newsitem.title: USA: Low inflation ensures growth/jobs - NY Fed's Mishkin.
newsitem.headline: Low inflation ensures growth/jobs - NY Fed's Mishkin.

text.p: Achieving low inflation is the only way for a central bank such as the Federal Reserve to contribute to long-term growth and job creation, New York Fed Director of Research Frederic Mishkin said on Tuesday.

"What a central bank can do is to provide the appropriate economic environment with low inflation which on the long run can produce jobs and can produce economic growth," Mishkin told the Money Marketeers of New York University.
Mishkin made the remarks as he presented his views on inflation targets and monetary policy.

"What we really care about is (to fight) inflation. It is our primary, overriding goal, not that this is the only thing we care about, but that this is in fact the overriding goal," Mishkin told the audience of economists.

"You hear criticism of central banks, like the Federal Reserve, that we are anti-growth. In fact, a central bank should be very pro-growth and indeed the way you get to be pro-growth is by creating an economic environment where businesses do what they are supposed to be doing," Mishkin also said.
Mishkin said targeting inflation helps "make a central bank accountable," and results in "increased transparency and increased accountability of a central bank."
Targeting inflation also helps address the fact "monetary policy operates with a lag, long lags" of up to two years, since an efficient policy "cannot wait until inflation" is apparent in price data.
